Subcapital fracture is the commonest type of intracapsular fracture of the proximal femur. The fracture line extends through the junction of the head and neck of femur.
· ·transcervical: midportion of femoral neck
basicervical: base of femoral neck

Subcapital and transcervical fractures are considered intracapsular fractures. While there is disagreement in the literature as to whether basicervical fractures are truly intracapsular or extracapsular, they should usually be treated like extracapsular fractures 14.
here are two distinct categories of femoral neck fractures: intracapsular fractures, including subcapital, transcervical, and basicervical fractures, and extracapsular peri-trochanteric fractures, which encompass intertrochanteric and subtrochanteric fractures. It is essential to differentiate between these types of fractures in order to provide the most appropriate treatment for each patient.

Technique: Multiplane multisequences of MRI of lumbo-sacral spine

Clinical notes : Low back pain with radiculopathy both lower limb.

Findings:

·	·Loss of lumbar lordosis is observed.

·	·No facet joint or flaval hypertrophy is seen at any level.

·	·No altered signal intensity is seen in spinal cord

·	·At L5/S1 level: Signal intensity of the disc is loss but maintaining the height of the disc.Diffuse disc bulge with mild paracentral disc herniation is seen ;resulting indentation on ventral thecal sac, mild narrowing of both neural foraminae and abutting traversing S1 nerve roots of both sides.

·	·At L4/L5 level: Signal intensity of the disc is loss but maintaining the height of the disc.Diffuse disc bulge with mild central and paracentral disc herniation is seen ;resulting in indentation on ventral thecal sac, mild narrowing of both neural foraminae and mild compression of traversing L5 nerve roots of both sides.

·	·At L1/L2, L2/L3 & L3/4 levels: Intervertebral discs show normal height and hydration. No evidence of disc bulge or protrusion is noted. No foraminal stenosis is noted.

Impression:

1. Suggestive of muscle spasm.

2. At L5/S1 level: Disc dessication and mild diffuse disc bulge with paracentral disc herniation causing narrowing of both neural foraminae and abutting traversing nerve roots of S1.

3. At L4/L5 level: Disc dessication and mild diffuse disc bulge with central and paracentral disc herniation causing narrowing of both neural foraminae and mild compression of traversing nerve roots of L5.
